summary: Snatch is a Go-based ransomware and data-extortion operation that has run since at least 2018 and that CISA/FBI described as still active in September 2023. It gets in through weak RDP (brute-forcing admin accounts), VPN services and credentials bought on criminal forums. It then moves to the domain controller, steals data through one-off services running batch scripts, and uses Cobalt Strike and Metasploit. Its hallmark is evading endpoint protection by registering its locker as a service under SafeBoot\Minimal, forcing a reboot into Safe Mode with bcdedit, deleting shadow copies and encrypting while security tools are not loaded.
uniqueTraits: Installs the locker as a service (for example SuperBackupMan, or randomised names) under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SafeBoot\Minimal, then 'bcdedit /set {current} safeboot minimal' and an immediate reboot
Exfiltrates through short-lived Windows services with random names that run batch files from the temp directory
Brute-forces RDP admin passwords, including on cloud (Azure) servers, and buys access from initial access brokers
Go binary packed with UPX, OpenPGP keys, 'HOW TO RESTORE YOUR FILES.TXT' note, C:\$SysReset folder

sources.title: Snatch ransomware reboots PCs into Safe Mode to bypass protection

chain.procedure: Connects through weak exposed RDP and VPN services, often with credentials bought on criminal forums. The group also recruits affiliates who already hold RDP, VNC or TeamViewer access.
chain.noAtomicReason: Purchased-credential logins through perimeter RDP/VPN cannot be reproduced on the endpoint. Validate with remote-access authentication analytics instead.

chain.procedure: Brute-forces RDP to get administrator credentials, for example on a Microsoft Azure server.

atomics.testName: Brute Force Credentials of single Active Directory domain users via SMB
atomics.note: Password-guesses a domain account over SMB, producing the same 4625 failure bursts.

atomics.testName: Brute Force Credentials of single Active Directory domain user via LDAP against domain controller (NTLM or Kerberos)
atomics.note: Password-guesses a domain account over LDAP.

chain.procedure: Uses the compromised admin account to RDP into a domain controller on the same network.

atomics.note: Opens an RDP session to a remote host with admin credentials.

chain.procedure: Holds C2 over port 443 to a Russian bulletproof-hosted VPS and uses Cobalt Strike reverse shells and Metasploit.

atomics.testName: Cobalt Strike post-exploitation pipe (4.2 and later)
atomics.note: Creates Cobalt Strike post-exploitation named pipes.
HTTP(S) C2 with suspicious user agents.

chain.procedure: Dumps WMIC system and user information and process lists, and records which users may log on to the machine. A custom Update_Collector.exe gathers WMI data for upload.

atomics.note: Enumerates users with WMIC.
Discovers processes with 'wmic process'.

chain.procedure: Queries the registry for system and software information.

atomics.note: Queries common registry keys with reg query.

chain.procedure: Runs Advanced Port Scanner to find more machines to target.

atomics.note: A PowerShell /24 port sweep that generates the same internal scan pattern.

chain.procedure: Dumps LSASS process memory and uploads the dump together with the user and process data.

atomics.note: Dumps LSASS with ProcDump.
Dumps LSASS with comsvcs.dll MiniDump.

chain.procedure: Tries to disable antivirus with Process Hacker, IObit Uninstaller, PowerTool, PsExec and DefenderControl.exe.

atomics.note: Disables a security service.
Disables Defender with a third-party utility (NirSoft AdvancedRun), the same class of tool as DefenderControl.
Runs Process Hacker, the tool Snatch used against AV processes.

chain.techniqueName: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
chain.procedure: Runs randomly named .bat files (for example evhgpp.bat) and deletes them afterwards.

atomics.note: Creates and runs a batch script.

atomics.testName: Delete a single file - Windows cmd
atomics.note: Deletes a file with cmd after it runs.

chain.techniqueName: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
chain.procedure: Uses sc.exe to create, query, start and stop services. One-off services with random names run batch files, and the locker is installed as a protected service (for example SuperBackupMan).

atomics.note: Installs a service with sc create.

atomics.testName: Execute a Command as a Service
atomics.note: Runs a command as a service.

chain.procedure: One-off services run batch files from %TEMP% that upload user account data, process lists, the LSASS dump and victim files to the C2 server before encryption.

atomics.note: Exfiltrates staged data over the C2 HTTP channel.

chain.procedure: Adds the locker's service (for example SuperBackupMan, mXoRpcSsx or VSS) under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SafeBoot\Minimal so it starts in Safe Mode.

atomics.testName: Windows Add Registry Value to Load Service in Safe Mode without Network
atomics.note: Adds a service under SafeBoot\Minimal (Safe Mode without networking).

atomics.testName: Windows Add Registry Value to Load Service in Safe Mode with Network
atomics.note: Adds a service under SafeBoot\Network.

chain.procedure: Runs 'bcdedit.exe /set {current} safeboot minimal' and then forces an immediate reboot with shutdown, so encryption happens in Safe Mode while EDR is not loaded.

atomics.note: Sets safeboot with bcdedit.
Forces an immediate restart.

chain.procedure: In Safe Mode, stops the service with net stop and deletes all shadow copies with 'vssadmin delete shadows /all /quiet'.

atomics.note: vssadmin delete shadows /all /quiet.

chain.procedure: Encrypts files with OpenPGP, skipping system and program folders, and appends a victim-specific hex or 5-character extension. It drops 'HOW TO RESTORE YOUR FILES.TXT'.

atomics.note: Drops a ransom note artifact.
Encrypts files with GPG4Win (OpenPGP), which matches Snatch's OpenPGP-based encryption.
